newsitem.title: INDIA: Peugeot to raise stake in India venture.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot to raise stake in India venture.

text.p: France's Peugeot Automobiles said on Saturday it wanted to raise by 50 percent its stake in an Indian joint venture with Premier Automobiles Ltd PAL).

"We are planning to pump in 920 million rupees, which will increase our stake to 47 percent from 32 percent currently held in the Indian joint venture," company spokesman J Manlay told reporters in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta.

The firm, PAL-Peugeot Ltd, is a 50:50 joint venture between Automobile Peugeot of France and India's PAL, in which each holds 32 percent of the equity, with the rest held by the public and financial institutions.
"We are negotiating with Premier Automobiles Ltd to increase our stake," said Manlay, PAL-Peugeot's deputy managing director.
"After we get the clearance from our Indian partner we will approach the FIPB for its approval for increasing our stake."
The Foreign Investment Promotion Board is a group set up by the Indian industry ministry to clear foreign investments up to six billion rupees.

Manlay said 500 million rupees of the projected investment would be used to offset losses incurred by labour troubles at the company's plant near Bombay, while the rest would be used to promote spare parts manufacturers.
Work at the Bombay plant, where the popular Peugeot 309 is assembled, came to a standstill last year after an employee agitation forced the management to declare a lock-out.
Production was affected for eight months before it reopened last October.
But the plant now produces 60 cars a day, Manlay said. The firm plans to manufacture 10,000 units of the 309 model in 1997 (January-December), rising to 27,000 in 1998.
